explanation: This is Stephan's Theorem C(i) in the quadratic case: if α > 1 is a root of X² − aX − b with nonzero conjugate β = a − α, |β| < 1, and A(α) = log2/logα + log2/log(1/|β|) < 1, then 10.61 holds at α. α > 2 is not assumed, but A < 1 forces α > 4 by C(ii). The hypotheses force α to be a quadratic Pisot number. The source is an unrefereed 2026 preprint, but a Lean proof is linked. The statement is consistent with the paper.
